title: You keep telling yourself you’re just being “real.”
paragraphs: You keep telling yourself you’re just being “real.”
That word has become your shield.
Your excuse.
Your hiding place.

You say, “I’m just being authentic,” but if you slow down long enough to really look… you already know something is off. Because deep down, there are moments when your “authentic self” doesn’t look like freedom.
It looks like compromise.
It looks like silence when you should have spoken truth.
It looks like indulging what you know God has already confronted.
God saw it.
You knew.
And yet you called it authenticity.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
Authenticity, by itself, is not a virtue in Scripture.
It’s not the highest good.
Because your “authentic self” is not neutral.
It’s fallen.
“The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?” (Jeremiah 17:9)
Read that again.
Deceitful. Not occasionally—above all things.
So when you say, “I’m just following my heart,” what you’re really saying is, “I’m trusting the very thing God warned me about.”
That’s not freedom.
That’s danger dressed as honesty.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
Now here’s where the tension tightens.
Because obedience feels… restrictive, doesn’t it?
It feels like losing yourself.
Like surrendering control.
Like becoming someone you didn’t choose.
And that’s exactly why you resist it.
You don’t want to be fake.
You don’t want to pretend.
You don’t want to perform religion.
So you swing to the other side and say, “I’d rather be real than obedient.”
But listen carefully.
Jesus never asked you to pretend.
He asked you to die.
“If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.” (Luke 9:23)
Not express yourself.
Deny yourself.
That’s where everything flips.
Because the real battle is not obedience versus authenticity.
It’s which “self” you’re being authentic to.
The one shaped by sin…
or the one reborn by grace.
Because Scripture doesn’t call you to suppress your identity—it calls you to receive a new one.
“Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.” (2 Corinthians 5:17)
So when obedience feels unnatural, it’s because it is.
To your old self.
And that’s the point.
There’s a version of you that feels right… and leads you away from God.
“There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.” (Proverbs 14:12)
That’s the version of you you’ve been protecting.
Defending.
Calling “authentic.”
But it’s killing you quietly.
Sin doesn’t always feel evil.
Sometimes it feels like you.
That’s why this is so dangerous.
Because you can be sincere… and still be wrong.
You can be honest… and still be in rebellion.
You can be authentic… and still be lost.
And then comes the breaking point.
When you realize that being true to yourself has not brought you peace.
It hasn’t healed the emptiness.
It hasn’t silenced the conviction.
Because deep down, you don’t just want to be real.
You want to be right with God.
And those are not the same thing.
So the question shifts.
Not “Am I being authentic?”
But “Am I surrendered?”
Because obedience is not about behavior management.
It’s about allegiance.
“If ye love me, keep my commandments.” (John 14:15)
Not perform.
Not pretend.
Love.
Real love obeys.
And here’s the part most people miss…
Obedience doesn’t erase your identity.
It restores it.
Because the truest version of you is not the one ruled by impulse.
It’s the one redeemed by Christ.
The one who doesn’t just follow feelings—but follows Jesus even when it costs.
That’s where real freedom is found.
Not in expressing everything you feel…
but in being transformed beyond what you feel.
“And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind…” (Romans 12:2)
Transformation requires tension.
It requires saying no to yourself.
It requires trusting God over your instincts.
And yes… it will feel like loss at first.
But what you lose is the version of you that was never meant to survive eternity.
And what you gain…
is life.
(Luke 9:24)
So which matters more—obedience or authenticity?
If authenticity means being true to your fallen nature…
then obedience must win.
Every time.
Because only obedience leads you to Jesus.
And only Jesus can make you truly new.
Not improved.
Not managed.
Reborn.
And now you’re standing in that quiet place again.
You feel it.
That pull.
That conviction.
That moment where you can either justify what you’ve been calling “authentic”…
or finally surrender it.
No one else is here.
No audience.
No performance.
Just you and God.
God saw it.
You knew.
And now you have to decide.
Say it plainly.
“I’ve been choosing myself over God.”
Type it if you have to.
Let it come into the light.
And if you’re ready to go deeper, to be corrected, sharpened, and grounded in the Word—not just inspired but transformed—you already know where this is leading.
